Approval to NCLP forThane and
Solapur
*421. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR:
SHRI DATTA MEGHE:
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government had accorded
approval to the National Child Labour Projects
under the Child Labour (P&R) Act, 1986 for
Thane and Solapur in 1995 and for 11 other
districts in the years 2003  and 2004;
(b) if so, the details thereof, the facilities
and support provided to child labour
thereunder and the number of children
covered in Maharashtra under the scheme;
(c) whether Government of
Maharashtra has proposed some more
districts in the State to be covered under
the National Child Labour Projects;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) Government's reaction thereto?
Provision of telephones in tribal
villages of Andhra Pradesh
*422. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether all the tribal villages have
been provided with telecommunication
facilities in Andhra Pradesh;
(b) if so, the details thereof, location-
wise and district-wise;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) whether Government have set any
target to provide said facilities to all the
tribal villages in Andhra Pradesh?
Exemption from toll tax
†*423. SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister of
SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND
HIGHWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government of
Rajasthan has requested for providing
exemption to the Parliamentarians and the
131

132

Legislators from payment of toll tax on
National Highways in Rajasthan; and
(b) if so, by when such exemption
would be provided?
Assistance sought by Karnataka
*424. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of SMALL
SCALE INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government of Karnataka
has sought assistance for upgradation of
existing Tool Room and Training Centre at
Hassan and for improvement of
productivity and quality of Kolhapuri
footwear cluster at Athani, Belgaum
district, under the Small Industry Cluster
Development Programme; and
(b) if so, the details in this regard and
the Central Government's reaction thereto?
Pending irrigation projects
†*425. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
SHRI JANARDAN DWIVEDI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) the details of pending irrigation
projects to make availability of water for
irrigation of agricultural land;
(b) the amount needed for remaining
period of Tenth Plan and the Eleventh Plan
period to solve the problems of pending
irrigation projects, development of waste
land and drought affected areas, State-wise;
(c) whether it is a fact that the States
have refused to contribute for big projects
in the meeting of the National Development
Council; and
(d) if so, in what manner Government
propose to manage and make provisions of
funds for the above projects?
Payment of compensation to Indians
by Myanmar
*426. MAULANA OBAIDULLAH
KHAN AZMI:
SHRI MOTIUR RAHMAN:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to refer to the answer
to Unstarred Question 2275 given in the
Rajya Sabha on 12th December, 2002 and
state:
(a) the details of meetings held between
India and Myanmar since 2003 onwards
on the issue of payment of compensation
to Indians by Myanmar;
(b) the details of cases settled and those
not settled, so far;
(c) the steps being taken for early
settlement of the remaining cases; and
(d) by when all the cases are likely to be
settled?
Privatisation of employment
exchanges
*427. SHRI MOOLCHAND
MEENA:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Planning Commission has
suggested privatising employment
exchanges and suggested that the
Employment Exchanges Act should be
amended to allow private employment
exchanges to provide jobs, placement
services to both private and public sector
establishments;
(b) if so, whether poor coverage of
employment exchances followed to capture
the chances in employment are the reasons
behind the proposal of the Commission;

133
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(c) if so, whether Government have
considered the proposal made by the
Planning Commission in their mid-term
appraisal; and
(d) if so, by when a final decision in this
regard is likely to be taken?
VPTs in Bihar
†*428. SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) the total number of inhabited villages
in Bihar on the basis of population in the
year 2001 and the number of villages where
the landline service has been made available
alongwith the total number of telephones
provided there; and
(b) the details of Government proposal
to make the telephone services available in
remaining villages which are without
landline telephones?
Mobile towers in Bulandshahr
†429. PROF. R.B.S. VARMA:
DR. CHHATTRAPAL SINGH
LODHA:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of applications seeking
mobile connection from B.S.N.L. lying
pending all over the country;
(b) the number of mobile towers
proposed by B.S.N.L. in Bulandshahr
district of Uttar Pradesh and by when these
would be set up; and
(c) the number of places in Bulandshahr
district where proposal for setting up of
mobile towers or telecom centres are under
consideration?
Talent from rural areas in sports
†*430. SHRI KAMAL AKHTAR: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that due to lack of
sufficient means of sports in the rural areas,
the country is deprived of emerging talents;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether Government have
formulated any plan to tap the talents from
the rural areas;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Funds allocated to sports schools
†*431. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) the amount allocated to the sports
schools during the last three years, State-
wise; and
(b) the names of schools which have
utilised full amount and whether the reasons
for not spending the amount have been
reviewed in case the abovesaid amount has
not been spent?
Rehabilitation of child labour
*432. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will
the Minister of LABOUR AND
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Mumbai
Police rescued more than 250 children by
raiding the premises of SSI units where they
were engaged as labour;

134
(b) if so, the details thereof including
those of the SSI units detected which had
engaged child labour and since when;
(c) the current status of the child
labourers, so rescued;
(d) the finding of survey conducted, if
any, of SSI and other units for detection of
child labour; and
(e) the details of the policy, if any, for
rehabilitation and subsistence of child labour
after their disengagement from occupations?
Revival of Hindustan Shipyard Ltd.
*433. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) the measures Government are taking
to revive the Hindustan Shipyard Ltd.;
(b) whether any proposal has been
submitted by the State Government of
Andhra Pradesh for revival of Hindustan
Shipyard;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether it is also a fact that
Hindustan Shipyard has recently got an
order to build 30,000 tonnes capacity DWT
bulk carrier ships; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Action against officers demanding
dowry
*434. SHRIMATI JAYA
BACHCHAN: Will the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
any media reports that in Rajasthan marriage
market, IAS, IPS and IRS officers command
the highest price at over Rs. one crore in
cash besides gold gifts and flashy weddings;
(b) whether this is in accordance with
Government's conduct rules; and
(c) if not, the steps Government
propose to bring home the provision in the
conduct rules and the concerned officers?
Coal reforms
*435. SHRI JESUDASU SEELAM:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to address the issue of coal sector reforms,
immediately;
(b) whether Finance Minister
addressing media has pointed out after stock
taking of Government's economic
performance a year after it came to power,
that power sector could not record higher
growth due to shortage of coal;
(c) if so, what are the proposed reforms
to be considered in regard to coal;
(d) whether any concrete policy has
been framed and prepared; and
(e) if so, the details thereof and by when
a final decision in starting coal reforms are
to be initiated?
Exploitation of Indian workers abroad
*436. SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to take measures to curb exploitation of
Indians taking up overseas employment;
(b) if so, whether Government have also
started taking stringent action against
recruiting agencies found guilty of cheating
Indians taken to the Gulf with promises of
employment;

135
(c) if so, whether the Minister during
his recent visit to UAE, his first hand feel
of condition of Indians had convinced him
that unscrupulous recruiting agencies were
responsible for miseries that some Indians,
especially labour class, face there; and
(d) if so, what steps Government have
taken or are likely to take to protect that
interests of Overseas Indians which are
being exploited in many countries?
Extradition treaty with Bangladesh
*437. SHRIMATI KUM KUM RAI:
SHRI R. KAMARAJ:
 Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether India and Bangladesh have
agreed on signing an extradition treaty
between them;
(b) if so, by when it has been planned
to implement the same;
(c) the details thereof; and
(d) if not, reasons therefor?
Nehru Yuva Kendras in Gujarat
*438. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA: Will the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) the number of  Nehru Yuva Kendras
functioning in Gujarat at present, location-
wise; and
(b) the details of the programmes run
by these Kendras during the last three years
and thereafter along with performance of
these Kendras in the State?
Upgradation of State Highways in
Tamil Nadu
*439. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have decided not to take up upgradation of
State Highways into National Highways;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor; and
(c) whether Government would
consider taking up National Highways
upgradation projects in Tamil Nadu in view
of the importance of the roads?
Registration of SSIs
†*440. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of SMALL SCALE
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that almost 70
percent units of small scale industries are
those where capital of less than five lacs
rupees has been invested;
(b) if not, the estimate of Government
in this regard;
(c) whether it is also a fact that majority
of these small scale industries are not even
registered;
(d) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto;
(e) whether Government have taken any
measures at national level to register all such
units; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?
NEW DELHI; YOGENDRA NARAIN,
The 19th August, 2005 Secretary-General.

(c) the action taken by Government
thereon;
(d) the total amount allocated to the
State for this purpose during each of the
last two years; and

and Orissa

decision?

recommendation of the Price Water House;

fixation of rates; and

supply gap;
(b) if so, the details of new projects
identified in different States; and
(c) by when, Government are likely to
start new projects?

station in Rajasthan

BAGRODIA:
SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
DR. PRABHA THAKUR:

to state:
(a) the reasons for reducing the coal
linkage for the power stations of Rajasthan
despite maintaining of PLF above 80-85
per cent by them; and

707
(b) what action are being taken by
Railway Board for transportation of coal
to the extent of full linkage quantity for the
power station of Rajasthan?
Demand of coal

PRASAD:
           DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER  be pleased
to state:
(a) whether any time-bound scheme has
been formulated with a fixed target to meet
the demand of coal in the country with the
coal produced indigenously;
(b) if so, the details in this regard;
(c) whether it is a fact that the demand
of coal can be fulfilled with the coal
produced indigenously by abolishing the
monopoly on Government coal; and
(d) if so, Government's reaction thereto?
Increase in the production of coal

REDDY:
SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
SHRI SURENDRA LATH:
Will the PRIME MINISTER  be pleased
to state:

has recast its production plan in order to
meet country's non-coking coal requirement

CIL would augment production to a
minimum of 20 MT every year beginning
from 2005-06;

production would increase to 363 MT by
2006-07 from 323 MT in 2004-05;
(d) if so, to what extent this production

during the year 2005?

Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL) propose
to develop 26 virgin coal blocks;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) how far this would enhance the
production capacity of the SECL and help
to bridge the gap between demand and
supply?

and
(c) if so, the details thereof?

demand-supply gap, Government are

of CIL

Will the PRIME MINISTER  be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a large number
of criminal cases and departmental enquiries
are pending against the officials
working with Coal India Limited as on 31st
July, 2005;
(b)  if so, the details thereof, company-
wise and category-wise;
(c) the number and names of the officers
suspended or continuing with their jobs,
company-wise; and
(d) the names of charge sheeted officers
to whom promotions have been given and
those who have not been given promotion
during the last three years?

mining

the PRIME MINISTER  be pleased to
state:

the formulation and implementation of a
policy regarding handing over the land

mining works to their owners after the

member?

SHRI MANOJ

the sale of its Earth station in VSNL

taken against the company  for unauthorised

services

the  Minister of  COMMUNICATIONS

be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the BSNL's
mobile base has crossed the one crore mark;

lucrative markets;
(c) if so, the reasons therefor;

technologies for broad band services; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?

Siwan in Bihar

the Minister of  COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that people of
Raghunathpur  have  to cover a  distance of
30 Kms. for sending a telegram to their
District H.Q. Siwan;
(b) whether Government have any
proposal to set up a Telegraph office at
Raghunathpur, Siwan (Bihar);

and
(d) if not, the reasons  therefor?

Minister of  COMMUNICATIONS AND
